# The blocking waits in runtime/v1 that TestRuntimeWaitsPark admits
# unparked. A row is `path<TAB>function<TAB>reason`; a row that admits no
# unparked wait fails the test. Every other blocking wait parks its task, so
# a clock's domain sees it (runtime.md, Machines and actors 11.16).

# a handshake: the wait ends when a task that runs reaches its next wait, so
# neither the clock nor the Advance's caller holds it; a Settle meanwhile
# only waits for the waiter to run on
runtime/v1/actor.go	machineStart	handshake: the caller waits until the new runner armed its first entry's timer and started its work (each a handshake below)
runtime/v1/actor.go	Actor.open	handshake: the runner waits until the entry's work filled its hosts, reached its first wait (rt.WhenWaiting) or ended
runtime/v1/actor.go	Actor.openFirst	handshake: the runner waits until the first entry's work filled its recovered hosts, reached its first wait (rt.WhenWaiting) or ended, as Actor.open does
runtime/v1/actor.go	Actor.arm	handshake: the runner waits until the timer child armed its sleep (rt.WhenWaiting) or ended

# a send that never waits
runtime/v1/actor.go	replySlot.give	no wait: the reply channel has room for its one answer; the asker is unparked first
runtime/v1/mailbox.go	mailSender.signal	no wait: wake has room for its one token; the sender is unparked first
runtime/v1/http.go	HTTPServe	no wait: served has room for Serve's one result
runtime/v1/http_client.go	httpDoURL	no wait: got has room for the exchange's one result
runtime/v1/rpc.go	RPCCall	no wait: got has room for the post's one result

# a goroutine of no task: no clock's domain holds it (batch 16d: the host
# waits of CU4, E4, CU6 and the RPC chain, which MK1's inventory predates)
runtime/v1/exec_start.go	newRunning	no task: the goroutine that closes chunks once the pipe readers end
runtime/v1/exec_start.go	Running.send	no task: a pipe reader goroutine hands a chunk to the reading task, or drops it once finish begins
runtime/v1/exec_start.go	hostProc.reap	no task: the reaper goroutine waits for the process's exit
runtime/v1/exec_start.go	ExecReplay	no task: the replay goroutine feeds the recorded chunks
runtime/v1/http.go	httpServer.ServeHTTP	no task: net/http's connection goroutine hands its call to the serve loop
runtime/v1/http_client.go	httpStreamRead	no task: the response reader goroutine hands an event to the reading task

# the host: the clock cannot see a process or an input (rt idle.go), so a
# wait on one keeps an Advance waiting until the host answers
runtime/v1/exec.go	ExecRun	host: the program's exit and output, and a reader's end
runtime/v1/host.go	lineReader.take	host: a line of standard input, or the reader's stop
runtime/v1/exec_start.go	Running.next	host: the next chunk of the program's output
runtime/v1/exec_start.go	Running.Wait	host: the program's exit
runtime/v1/exec_start.go	Running.end	host: the program's exit within its grace
runtime/v1/exec_start.go	Running.finish	host: the pipe readers' end within the wait delay
runtime/v1/http_client.go	httpStreamURL	host: the next event of a streamed response
runtime/v1/http_client.go	httpRefusedStatus	host: the next event of a refused response's body
runtime/v1/rpc.go	rpcCalls	host: the end of a call that a network request started
runtime/v1/rpc.go	rpcRun.stopAll	host: the end of each call left, which a network request started
runtime/v1/rpc.go	rpcRun.end	host: the handle of a call that ended; it has ended, so the wait returns
runtime/v1/rpc.go	rpcRun.start	handshake: a call task waits until its spawner set its handle, then hands its end to the serve loop

# a wait that parks inside runtime/rt
runtime/v1/task.go	Task.Wait	parks in rt: rt.Handle.Wait parks the owner on the handle (rt handle.go)
